summary: The old trade road east from Kalimpong to Pedong, the last bazaar before the Jelep La caravans climbed into Sikkim and Tibet. About 20 km and an hour by shared jeep through Algarah, with Sillery Gaon and Damsang fort a short hop beyond.

options.text: Shared jeeps to Pedong leave from Kalimpong's Motor Stand through the morning and early afternoon, filling up before they go. The road runs through Algarah and along the ridge with views north into Sikkim. The last jeeps back from Pedong leave by mid-afternoon, so do not plan a late return. Change at Pedong for Sillery Gaon or hire a local car.

A reserved car from the Motor Stand or your hotel is the easy option with luggage or a family. Ask for a half-day package that adds Damsang fort, Sangchen Dorjee monastery and Cross Hill for around ₹2,500–3,500. Drivers know the road well; agree the price and stops before you set off.

Walkers can take a shared jeep to Algarah and walk some of the old trade path on village trails towards Pedong, with a local guide. It is a half-day ramble through cardamom, maize and broom grass, and gives a real sense of the mule route. Avoid it in the monsoon, when paths are slippery and leeches are out.

stops_on_way: Algarah bazaar for tea and a look at the ridge
Viewpoints over the Rishi and Teesta valleys towards Sikkim
Sangchen Dorjee monastery just before Pedong
tip: Leave Kalimpong by 9 am so you have time for Damsang fort and the monastery before the afternoon cloud and the last jeep back.

faqs.q: How far is Pedong from Kalimpong?
faqs.a: Pedong is about 20 km east of Kalimpong, a drive of roughly 45 minutes to 1.25 hours depending on the vehicle and traffic at Algarah. Shared jeeps cost ₹80–120 a seat and leave from the Kalimpong Motor Stand. A reserved car costs about ₹1,500–2,200 one way.

faqs.q: Can I visit Pedong as a day trip from Kalimpong?
faqs.a: Yes. Leave around 9 am, see Sangchen Dorjee monastery, Cross Hill and Damsang fort, eat lunch in Pedong bazaar and return by mid-afternoon. With a reserved car you can add Sillery Gaon or Ramitey Dara. To see sunrise from the ridges, stay a night in Sillery Gaon or Icchey Gaon instead.

faqs.q: Was Pedong on the Silk Route?
faqs.a: Pedong was on the Kalimpong–Lhasa trade road over Jelep La, which carried Tibetan wool and goods until the 1962 war closed the pass. Travellers often call the whole network the Silk Route. The better-known Silk Route drive today runs through Rongli and Zuluk in East Sikkim, on the other side of the Rishi river.

faqs.q: Is the Kalimpong–Pedong road open in the monsoon?
faqs.a: The road is usually open in the monsoon but can be blocked for hours by landslides after heavy rain, especially from July to September. Start early, carry snacks and keep a buffer day if you are connecting to a train or flight. Check current status before you travel.

summary: From Kalimpong east through Algarah to Lava, then down a forest road to the Lepcha village of Lolegaon. About 55 km and 2.5–3 hours, with the Lava monastery and a tea stop at the halfway point.

options.text: Most travellers hire a car from Kalimpong, which lets you stop at Algarah, Lava's Kagyu Thekchen Ling monastery and the viewpoints on the way. If you are going on to Charkhole or back via Lava, a two-day car package works out cheaper per day. Agree the stops and waiting time before you leave.

Take a shared jeep from Kalimpong's Motor Stand to Lava (₹120–180, mostly mornings), then a shared or reserved vehicle from Lava to Lolegaon. Shared jeeps on the Lava–Lolegaon stretch are few and irregular; be ready to pay ₹1,800–2,500 for a car if nothing is going. This option suits backpackers with a flexible day.

If you only want to see the canopy walk and Jhandi Dara, a full-day round trip from Kalimpong is possible but long. We prefer at least one night at Lolegaon, which gives you a dawn at Jhandi Dara and a quiet morning in the heritage forest.

stops_on_way: Kagyu Thekchen Ling monastery at Lava
Forest stretches between Lava and Lolegaon, good for birds
tip: Stop at Lava for lunch going out, because Lolegaon has few places to eat outside the homestays and the forest lodge.

faqs.q: How far is Lolegaon from Kalimpong?
faqs.a: Lolegaon is about 55 km from Kalimpong, via Algarah and Lava, and takes 2.5–3 hours by car. Lava is roughly halfway, about 30 km from Kalimpong and 24 km from Lolegaon. A reserved car costs ₹3,000–4,000 one way; shared jeeps run to Lava, but are rare beyond it.

faqs.q: Can I go from Kalimpong to Lolegaon by shared jeep?
faqs.a: Partly. Shared jeeps run from Kalimpong to Lava, mostly in the morning. From Lava to Lolegaon there are only occasional shared vehicles, so you may need to hire a car for ₹1,800–2,500. Ask at Lava's jeep stand and leave Kalimpong early to keep your options open.

faqs.q: Is the Lava–Lolegaon road good?
faqs.a: It is a narrow hill road through forest, mostly paved, with some rough patches and landslide-prone stretches in the monsoon. Small cars manage in the dry season. After heavy rain, expect delays and occasional blocks. Check current status before you travel, especially from July to September.

faqs.q: Should I visit Lava or Lolegaon first?
faqs.a: From Kalimpong it makes sense to go to Lava first, since it is on the way, then continue to Lolegaon. Many travellers then return to Siliguri directly from Lolegaon through Gorubathan or via Kalimpong, depending on the roads. Check current status before you travel, as NH10 closures change the best way down.

summary: Siliguri to Lava either through Kalimpong on NH10 and Algarah, or through the Dooars via Gorubathan, the road that matters when NH10 is shut. About 100–110 km and 4–5 hours either way.

options.text: Take a shared jeep from Siliguri to Kalimpong (₹200–300, 3–3.5 h), then a shared jeep from Kalimpong's Motor Stand to Lava (₹120–180, 1.5 h). The second leg runs mostly in the morning, so you may need to sleep in Kalimpong. NH10 between Sevoke and Teesta Bazar has had repeated closures since October 2023: check current status before you travel.

Through the Dooars: Sevoke, across the Teesta to Odlabari or Malbazar, then up through Gorubathan to Lava. This road, upgraded as an alternative to NH10, avoids the Teesta gorge. It climbs through tea gardens and forest and is steep near the top. Drivers choose between the two routes on the day depending on landslides.

The classic road: NH10 up the Teesta to Teesta Bazar, climb to Kalimpong, then east through Algarah to Lava. It lets you break the journey in Kalimpong for lunch or a night. Use it when NH10 is open, and check current status before you travel.

stops_on_way: Coronation Bridge at Sevoke over the Teesta
Teesta Bazar or the Dooars tea gardens, depending on the route
tip: Ask your driver the evening before which road is open, because NH10 and the Gorubathan road can each be blocked after rain.

faqs.q: How do I get from Siliguri to Lava?
faqs.a: The simplest way is a reserved car from NJP, Bagdogra or Siliguri for ₹4,500–6,000, which takes 4–5 hours via Kalimpong or via Gorubathan in the Dooars. On a budget, take a shared jeep to Kalimpong and another to Lava the next morning. Check current status before you travel, because NH10 has had frequent closures since 2023.

faqs.q: Is there a direct shared jeep from Siliguri to Lava?
faqs.a: Direct shared jeeps are rare and not reliable. Most budget travellers change at Kalimpong, where morning jeeps leave for Lava from the Motor Stand. If you arrive in Kalimpong after midday, plan to sleep there. Ask at the Siliguri jeep stands on the day, as services change.

faqs.q: Which is better: via Kalimpong or via Gorubathan?
faqs.a: When NH10 is open, the Kalimpong road lets you break the trip and is well served by jeeps. When NH10 is closed or slow, the Gorubathan road through the Dooars avoids the Teesta gorge entirely. Drivers decide on the day. Allow 4–5 hours either way, and check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is NH10 open to Kalimpong now?
faqs.a: NH10 between Sevoke and Rangpo has had many closures since the October 2023 Teesta flood, including a major landslide near Coronation Bridge in June 2026. It reopens and closes with repairs and weather. Before you travel, ask your hotel or driver and check local news and police updates for the day.

summary: Down from the Lava forests through Gorubathan to the tea gardens and grasslands of the Dooars, for a hills-and-jungle trip in one go. About 80 km and 3–3.5 hours to Lataguri, the village at the Gorumara gate.

options.text: The practical way. The road drops from about 2,200 m at Lava through forest and Gorubathan to the plains near Malbazar, then runs east to Lataguri. Expect hairpins in the first hour and a straight road at the end. Drivers often stop at a tea garden or a riverbed on the way. Check current status before you travel in the monsoon.

Possible for backpackers with time: shared jeep from Lava down to Gorubathan or Malbazar when one is going, then a bus or shared auto to Lataguri. Services are thin and irregular, so leave Lava early and ask at the jeep stand the evening before.

stops_on_way: Forest stretches below Lava for birds
tip: Remember that Gorumara National Park closes for the monsoon, roughly mid-June to mid-September, so time this route for the dry months.

faqs.q: How far is Gorumara from Lava?
faqs.a: Lataguri, the main village at the edge of Gorumara National Park, is about 80 km from Lava. The drive takes about 3–3.5 hours by car through Gorubathan and Malbazar, and a reserved car costs roughly ₹4,000–5,500. Safari bookings are separate and must be made in advance.

faqs.q: Can I combine Lava with a Dooars safari?
faqs.a: Yes, and it makes a good contrast: two nights in the Lava forests at about 2,200 m, then two in the Dooars grasslands near 100 m. Gorumara closes for the monsoon, roughly mid-June to mid-September, and safari rules change. Book your jungle safari in advance and check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is the Lava–Gorubathan road safe?
faqs.a: It is a steep, narrow hill road with many bends, used daily by local jeeps and trucks. In dry weather it is fine with a local driver. In the monsoon, landslides and fog can slow it down. Avoid driving it after dark and check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is Gorubathan a good alternative to NH10?
faqs.a: Often, yes. When NH10 along the Teesta is closed, the road from the Dooars through Gorubathan to Lava, upgraded as an alternative route, is how many people reach Lava and even Kalimpong. It takes longer to Kalimpong, but avoids the Teesta gorge. Check current status before you travel.

summary: From Pedong down to the Reshi river, across the West Bengal–Sikkim border and up to Aritar's lake in East Sikkim. About 30 km and 1.5 hours, on roads the old Tibet caravans once used.

options.text: The road drops from Pedong to the Reshi bridge on the border, enters Sikkim, then climbs through Rhenock to Aritar. A Kalimpong-registered car can make the run; ask your driver about Sikkim entry rules for the vehicle. Indian visitors show an ID at the check post. Check current status before you travel.

Possible but slow: a shared jeep from Pedong towards Reshi or Rhenock when one is going, then a local jeep up to Aritar. Services are irregular, so start in the morning. This suits backpackers who are already in Pedong or Sillery Gaon and heading on into Sikkim.

stops_on_way: Reshi bridge on the Bengal–Sikkim border
Rhenock bazaar on the old trade route
tip: Foreign nationals need a Sikkim Restricted Area Permit before they cross; arrange it in advance rather than counting on getting it at the Reshi check post.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to go from Pedong to Aritar?
faqs.a: Indian nationals do not need a permit to enter this part of Sikkim, only a photo ID at the check post. Foreign nationals need a Sikkim Restricted Area Permit, which is easier to arrange in advance or at the main entry points than at small posts like Reshi. Rules change, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How long does Pedong to Aritar take?
faqs.a: About 1.5 hours by car for roughly 30 km: down to the Reshi river on the border, then up through Rhenock to Aritar. By shared jeep with changes, expect 2–3 hours. Landslides in the monsoon can add time, so check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can I combine Kalimpong and the Silk Route via Pedong?
faqs.a: Yes. Pedong and Reshi lead into East Sikkim at Rhenock, the start of the drive to Rongli, Zuluk and the old Silk Route. That stretch needs a separate permit for all visitors, arranged through registered operators. Pedong to Aritar is a good first stop on the way.

faqs.q: Was this the old trade route to Tibet?
faqs.a: Roughly, yes. Mule caravans from Kalimpong came through Pedong and Rhenock and climbed to Jelep La, then into Tibet's Chumbi valley, carrying wool south and goods north until the 1962 war closed the pass. Today's roads follow parts of that line, though not the old mule path itself.
